THE EXPLORATION ARCHIVE / 1957–2021

Before it was history,
it was the unknown.

From the first satellite to telescopes that look into the distant past. Explore 15 selected milestones—and the details behind them.

15 selected milestones4 threads of exploration1 shared curiosity

15 milestones · oldest first

  1. 195704 OCT 1957
    ROBOTIC EXPLORATION

    Sputnik 1 opens the Space Age

    The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite into Earth orbit. A small spacecraft became a turning point in global exploration.

    Behind the milestone +

    A satellite before a passenger

    The first satellite preceded the first human spaceflight by less than four years.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  2. 195801 OCT 1958
    INSTITUTIONS

    NASA begins operations

    The United States’ new civilian space agency began work, building on the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics.

    Behind the milestone +

    The first A matters

    NASA’s remit includes aeronautics: research into flight within Earth’s atmosphere, as well as beyond it.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  3. 196112 APR 1961
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth

    Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space during the Vostok 1 mission.

    Behind the milestone +

    A 108-minute milestone

    Gagarin’s flight lasted 108 minutes. He ejected from the returning capsule and landed by parachute.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  4. 196316 JUN 1963
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Valentina Tereshkova makes history

    Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6, becoming the first woman to travel into space.

    Behind the milestone +

    More than a single orbit

    Her mission completed 48 orbits of Earth over nearly three days.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  5. 196518 MAR 1965
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    The first spacewalk

    Alexei Leonov left Voskhod 2 to become the first person to conduct a spacewalk.

    Behind the milestone +

    A new kind of work

    Leaving a spacecraft created a new engineering challenge: the suit had to function as a personal pressurized environment.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  6. 196824 DEC 1968
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Apollo 8 reaches lunar orbit

    Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first humans to orbit the Moon.

    Behind the milestone +

    Looking back changed the view

    During the mission, Anders photographed the famous color Earthrise image above the lunar horizon.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  7. 196920 JUL 1969
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Apollo 11 lands on the Moon

    The lunar module Eagle landed with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin aboard. Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.

    Behind the milestone +

    Landing and walking are different moments

    The landing occurred on July 20 UTC. Armstrong’s first step followed on July 21 UTC—still July 20 in the eastern United States.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  8. 197620 JUL 1976
    ROBOTIC EXPLORATION

    Viking 1 works on Mars

    NASA’s Viking 1 made the first successful U.S. landing on Mars and returned photographs from the surface.

    Behind the milestone +

    A familiar anniversary

    Viking 1 touched down seven years to the day after Apollo 11’s lunar landing.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  9. 197705 SEP 1977
    ROBOTIC EXPLORATION

    Voyager 1 begins its journey

    Voyager 1 launched toward Jupiter and Saturn, beginning a voyage that would eventually take it into interstellar space.

    Behind the milestone +

    A message travels with it

    The spacecraft carries a Golden Record of sounds and images representing Earth. Voyager 2 carries one, too.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  10. 198318 JUN 1983
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Sally Ride flies on Challenger

    Ride became the first American woman in space as a mission specialist aboard STS-7.

    Behind the milestone +

    A physicist in orbit

    Her work included helping develop and operate the Shuttle’s robotic arm.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  11. 199024 APR 1990
    OBSERVATORIES

    Hubble launches

    Space Shuttle Discovery carried the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit, opening a new chapter in astronomy.

    Behind the milestone +

    An observatory built to be visited

    Astronauts later serviced Hubble, repairing equipment and improving its scientific instruments.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  12. 199212 SEP 1992
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Mae Jemison reaches orbit

    Jemison became the first African American woman in space aboard Endeavour’s STS-47 mission.

    Behind the milestone +

    Medicine, engineering and exploration

    A physician and engineer, she worked on a research mission involving life sciences and materials science.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  13. 202030 MAY 2020
    HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT

    Crew Dragon’s first astronaut launch

    Demo-2 carried Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley toward the International Space Station in a test of SpaceX’s crew transportation system.

    Behind the milestone +

    A demonstration from start to finish

    The mission tested the system from launch through docking, departure and return to Earth.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  14. 202118 FEB 2021
    ROBOTIC EXPLORATION

    Perseverance lands in Jezero

    NASA’s rover arrived at a Martian crater with evidence of an ancient lake and delta, to investigate the planet’s past.

    Behind the milestone +

    Rocks as a historical record

    Its samples preserve clues to Mars’s geological and environmental history, for possible future study on Earth.

    Read the source · NASA ↗
  15. 202125 DEC 2021
    OBSERVATORIES

    Webb heads into space

    The James Webb Space Telescope launched aboard an Ariane 5, beginning its journey toward an observing orbit around the Sun–Earth L2 region.

    Behind the milestone +

    A telescope that had to unfold

    Its segmented mirror and five-layer sunshield were folded for launch and deployed in space.

    Read the source · NASA ↗

A selected timeline, not a complete history. Dates identify the event described. When a milestone crosses calendar days in different time zones, the note explains the distinction.
